scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You put on noise cancelling earphones, and the bus engine just disappears. But what actually happens?

scenes.name: sound
scenes.text: Sound is just air pressure going up and down, a wave. Your eardrum feels those pushes and pulls.

scenes.name: mic
scenes.text: A tiny microphone on the outside of each earbud hears the noise before it reaches your ear.

scenes.name: flip
scenes.text: A chip inside computes the exact opposite wave. Where the noise pushes, the new wave pulls.

scenes.name: play
scenes.text: The speaker plays that anti noise along with your music, within a fraction of a millisecond.

scenes.name: cancel
scenes.text: The two waves meet in your ear canal and cancel out. A second mic inside checks what's left, and corrects it.

scenes.name: limits
scenes.text: It works best on steady, low sounds, like engines and hum. Sudden or high sounds, like voices, are mostly blocked by the ear tip seal.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Listen, flip, play, cancel. Silence, made from sound. Follow for more on how things really work.
